title: Stimulus direction and orientation angle convention shared by Citrus and Palette
status: draft: Citrus implementation pending; no admitted catalog uses it yet

authority.surveyed_at: Citrus main 53b68a7; agent-contracts origin/main 9e37316; Palette main ba5a78a
authority.enforcement: src/stimuli/angle_convention.h (planned): UnitCircleDegreesToYDownVector, YDownVectorToUnitCircleDegrees; a source-scan test refuses any other degrees-to-vector conversion under src/stimuli/

consumers.artifact: import_stimulus_to_zarr (record the convention per admission binding; stop treating the authored angle as a camera angle)
stimulus_response_grating and stimulus_response_omr (compare heading to stimulus direction by mapping the direction vector through the homography, never by subtracting angles)
stimulus step reads, via Palette only (Palette docs/crimson_stimulus_step_read_contract.md); Crimson never reads Citrus angles directly

angle.same_id_as: citrus-palette/heading/heading_convention_v1.json angle.id; the id names a rule for any y-down raster, and heading v1 is one instance of it (the source-camera raster)
angle.applies_to: any y-down raster: stimulus canvas, arena-relative canvas, camera view. The raster is named by the field's frame (field name suffix or direction_reference_frame), never by the angle id.
angle.angle_to_vector: theta_deg names the unit vector (cos(theta), -sin(theta)) in the raster, theta in radians = radians(theta_deg)
angle.positive_rotation: counter-clockwise as seen on the image (+90 = up on the raster)

range.rule: Authored and recorded values are finite degrees and are NOT normalised: 270, -90 and 630 are all legal and name the same direction. Non-finite values are refused. Vector-to-angle results lie in [-180, 180]; -180 and +180 are the same direction (atan2(-0.0, negative) = -180 in IEEE arithmetic).
range.compare: two angles a and b in the same raster agree when |wrap_delta(a - b)| <= tolerance; never raw equality
range.mod: floored modulo with result in [0, 360) (Python %); C/C++ fmod truncates toward zero and needs +360 on a negative result

plane.rule: The convention is per raster. An angle never crosses rasters by number: never subtract or add a canvas angle and a camera angle. To compare a canvas direction with a camera direction (for example a fish heading), convert the angle to its vector in the source raster, map the VECTOR through the local Jacobian of the homography at the relevant point (camera->canvas, or its inverse for canvas->camera), and take the angle of the mapped vector in the destination raster. The homography's determinant sign carries the rig's reflection: det < 0 reverses rotation sense, so a canvas-up direction is camera-down on a y-reflected rig.
plane.jacobian: for H = [[h00,h01,h02],[h10,h11,h12],[h20,h21,h22]] at source point (x, y): w = h20 x + h21 y + h22, u = (h00 x + h01 y + h02) / w, v = (h10 x + h11 y + h12) / w; J = [[(h00 - u h20)/w, (h01 - u h21)/w], [(h10 - v h20)/w, (h11 - v h21)/w]]; mapped vector = J * (vx, vy)
plane.reflection: sign(det J) = sign(det H) * sign(w)^3; det J < 0 means the rig mirrors the raster
plane.same_rule_as: heading_convention_v1.json projection.rule (two points mapped through the homography, which is the finite-difference form of the Jacobian map)
plane.known_violation: Palette stimulus_response_grating.py:126-133 subtracts the legacy clockwise canvas angle from the counter-clockwise camera heading; it is right only on a reflected rig (omnifin0, det < 0). Fixing it is required for both legacy and v1 bindings.

declared_in.note: beside software_version; one attribute per session, never per stimulus table, chaser attribute or field

declared_in.requires: schema_id citrus.stimulus_protocol, schema_version 2; a file with no top-level version is legacy version 1 (clockwise) and is refused by the loader
envelope policy citrus.protocol.semantic.v2; every protocol's hash changes, including angle-free protocols

legacy.definition: 0 = +x (right), +90 = down on the raster, positive clockwise on the image; vector (cos(theta), sin(theta)); angle degrees(atan2(y, x))
legacy.conversion: theta_v1 = -theta_legacy (same raster, same vector); compare under wrap_delta
legacy.classification: by admission catalog binding, never by the session attribute. A file without catalog_id, or bound to one of the catalogs above, is canvas_y_down_clockwise_legacy. A file whose binding selects a catalog admitted under this convention but lacks or contradicts the /metadata/session attribute is refused (catalog_id_mismatch precedent).
legacy.admission: the per-catalog pin field and the new catalog belong to a later unified H5 admission revision; this document does not create one

moving_grating_drift_rule.note: Amends qa/answers/citrus-to-palette/Q-20260302-1258-grating-orientation-answer.yaml, which named orientation_degrees as the grating axis but did not state the drift relation.
moving_grating_drift_rule.orientation_era: Protocol files before Citrus c8c146b (2026-04-17) carry orientation_degrees (the render axis, the grating normal) and a signed speed_pps, no motion_direction_degrees. The kernel is pos = x*cos(axis) + y*sin(axis) with phase increasing at +speed, so the pattern drifts toward -axis: drift_deg = orientation_degrees + 180 when speed_pps > 0, drift_deg = orientation_degrees when speed_pps < 0. Clockwise, +90 = down.
moving_grating_drift_rule.motion_direction_era: From c8c146b (2026-04-17) until the unit-circle switch, files carry motion_direction_degrees (+ direction_reference_frame, default STIMULUS_CANVAS) and not orientation_degrees; motion_direction_degrees IS the drift direction (clockwise, +90 = down; CAMERA_VIEW values map through the Jacobian). Citrus derived orientation_degrees = motion + 180 at positive speed on load and never wrote it back.
moving_grating_drift_rule.unit_circle_era: From citrus.stimulus_protocol schema_version 2: motion_direction_degrees is the drift direction under atan2_negative_y_x_degrees (+90 = up), finite, unnormalised.
moving_grating_drift_rule.zero_speed: speed_pps == 0 in any era: the grating is static and has no drift direction. Consumers record it as static and refuse to assign a direction; they never pick one.
moving_grating_drift_rule.motion_era_negative_speed: In the motion era (and the unit-circle era) motion_direction_degrees is the drift for either sign of speed_pps: Citrus derives the render axis as motion + 180 when speed_pps >= 0 and motion when speed_pps < 0, so the sign is absorbed by the axis, never by the drift. The orientation-era flip applies only to files that carry orientation_degrees without motion_direction_degrees.
